name: John Johnson
role: Hiram farmer who hosted Joseph Smith
dateNote: Joseph Smith lived in his Hiram home in 1831–1832; he joined the United Firm on 4 June 1833.
importance: Joseph Smith lived and received many revelations in his home at Hiram, Ohio. Section 96 accepts his offering and admits him to the United Firm in June 1833. Section 102 names him to the first Kirtland high council, and section 104 assigns him property. He became disaffected from the Church in 1837–1838.
connections: He married Alice (Elsa) Jacobs in 1800. He was the father of Lyman and Luke Johnson.

sources.title: John Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 11 Apr. 1778, Chesterfield, New Hampshire; settled at Hiram 1818; baptized c. 1831; moved to Kirtland 1833; United Firm 4 June 1833; Kirtland high council 1834–1837; disaffected 1837–1838; died 30 July 1843, Kirtland (year inferred by JSP from an obituary).
